entities.name: PMID:27519149
observations: In paired donated human corneal-section mock grafts cultured for 2 days, collagen cross-linking increased failure stress to 0.691 ± 0.12 mPa versus 0.236 ± 0.09 mPa untreated; paired p=0.0087.
The study concluded that collagen cross-linking promoted early adhesion between separate corneal sections.

entities.name: PMID:23960934
observations: In ex vivo human corneal graft models, femtosecond UVA-riboflavin cross-linking increased PKP burst pressure by 31.32 mmHg versus control (p<0.05).
Cross-linked ALK donor-recipient specimens had separation strength of 954.7 ± 290.4 kPa, supporting stronger graft-interface attachment.

entities.name: PMID:37126648
observations: In ex vivo corneal perforation and lamellar keratectomy models, riboflavin/UVA-crosslinked collagen gel formed a cohesive interface and sealed defects in a burst assay.
The abstract did not provide a direct quantitative adhesion comparison sufficient to classify the treatment effect definitively.

entities.name: Mock graft adhesion increase
observations: In a human mock corneal graft model, collagen cross-linking significantly increased the force/stress required to separate paired corneal sections compared with untreated controls.
